question: How does What's Desired combine permanent Lakshana damage with a refreshed self CRIT damage buff on Skill/Ultimate admission?
decision: Apply the permanent refinement ratio to delivered Lakshana packets only. Successful native Skill or Ultimate admission refreshes one wearer CRIT damage modifier before same-time hits; duration is world-time and independent from switching. Use the existing cast-buff-order hypothesis and shared BuffManager; failed admission gives no buff.
availability: Frozen Global release availability remains unverified.
stop_condition: Check all three T1-T5 curves/units, element/cast classification independence, independent noncritical/critical damage arithmetic, refresh/nonstacking/equal-time expiry, failed admission and off-field ownership, legal compatible Chaos build and CLI/WASM/Worker parity.
return_condition: New cast order, snapshot, clock, element or release evidence conflicts with the model.
checks: 174 content tests pass. Native T1-T5 bind .20/.25/.30/.35/.40 Lakshana, .40/.50/.60/.70/.80 CRIT damage and 20 seconds; changed duration units fail. Legal A0 Chaos Skill build matches an independent additive-zone ratio including existing Warrant +.20.

Independent synthetic oracle: 1000 ATK * .5 DEF * (1 + .1 general + .2 Lakshana) * (1 + 1 native CD + .4 active CD). Nature Skill uses only CRIT damage; normal Lakshana uses permanent bonus; Skill/Ultimate refresh never stacks; exact expiry at 25 seconds removes CRIT damage before the hit. Noncritical hits ignore the CRIT damage buff. Delayed hits sample current state at delivery, including exact expiry and off-field ownership; the active ally receives neither modifier. Failed admission grants no buff; duplicate/wrong equipment/zero-duration configs fail.

Public Chaos T1-T5 runs native primary Attack/Skill/Ultimate packets with 100% CRIT (.05 character + .24 weapon + .71 explicit stat). Hits at 0/.8/2/21.999999/22.799999 seconds independently verify permanent damage, existing Warrant, refreshed CRIT damage and expiry. Full native CLI/WASM reports agree for all five scripts; actual Worker T5 matches direct WASM. Mint compatibility is rejected.

TypeScript and production build, native_build and scenario_script modules pass. Changed Rust formatting passes. Content clippy passes with only the two pre-existing metadata lints collapsible_if and single_element_loop allowed. Native parity uses NTESIM_VERIFY_NATIVE=1 NTESIM_VERIFY_WEAPON=gold; existing weapons retain direct WASM/Worker coverage.

Chaos primary adapters select first frozen ordinary/Skill/Ultimate packets and validate GAName membership in the native catalog.
